answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a quill as the anchor of the cost.
